summary: 112 claims citing 87 links; quotes: 11 (7 word for word, 4 missing); links: 83 read, 1 unreadable, 1 refused, 2 gone; 1 with no Wayback record.

claims.text: In the first stage ("memory proposes"), the model's parametric familiarity with a brand sets the default consideration set: with identical specifications a recognized brand beat nine spec-identical fictional rivals in 100% of 670 trials across GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet and Gemini 3 Flash (Chu & Hou, arXiv 2606.17443).

One Wirecutter screenshot did shift a frontier agent's pick by +99 points (Wharton GAIL, Aug 2026), yet Wirecutter appears in only ~10% of "best product" answers (vendor data), official brand sites still supply 46.4% of ChatGPT citations even on comparison queries (Ahrefs), and only 15.2% of ChatGPT product categories have a settled "owner" (Semrush).
Every official statement is a list of factors without weights, and OpenAI's own feed spec says eligibility "does not guarantee display" (OpenAI Product Feed Spec).

The most revealing official admission is OpenAI's April 2025 statement that product selection considers "ChatGPT's earlier model responses, before new search results" alongside third-party metadata and reviews (PPC Land), which is a direct acknowledgement that parametric knowledge is an explicit input.

quotes.quote: ChatGPT's earlier model responses, before new search results

claims.text: Stage: 1. Query interpretation and personalization | What happens: Model parses intent, budget, dislikes, Memory and custom instructions | Documented or inferred: Documented (OpenAI, Amazon, Google) | Key measured drivers: Stated budget shifts weighting to price; a stated dislike filters products out; a one-sentence user memory can redirect the pick | Representative evidence: OpenAI Help; Wharton GAIL

Stage: 2. Prior-driven candidate generation | What happens: Model names brands from parametric memory before or without retrieval | Documented or inferred: Inferred, measured | Key measured drivers: Brand familiarity (100% incumbent win on ties); training-data frequency; popularity | Representative evidence: arXiv 2606.17443; Hou et al.

Stage: 3. Retrieval and source selection | What happens: Query fan-out across web search, Google Shopping, feeds, catalog; model selects which pages to trust and quote | Documented or inferred: Partly documented (fan-out, feeds); source weighting inferred | Key measured drivers: Platform-specific source mixes; licensing deals (ChatGPT only); quotability of passages; position in context | Representative evidence: Google Search Central; Semrush; C-SEO Bench

Stage: 4. Shortlist synthesis | What happens: Model merges priors and retrieved evidence into 1–5 named products | Documented or inferred: Inferred, measured | Key measured drivers: Stochastic sampling; a stable "head" of 2–4 brands per category; model-specific modal products | Representative evidence: SparkToro; arXiv 2609.05059

Stage: 5. Final pick | What happens: Agent selects one item from a grid, list or set of offers | Documented or inferred: Inferred, measured in sandboxes | Key measured drivers: Grid position (5×), platform badges (2–4×), "Sponsored" penalty, star rating (+0.1 star matters), review count, price, first adequate offer | Representative evidence: ACES, arXiv 2508.02630; Magentic Marketplace

Stage: 6. Merchant selection and checkout | What happens: Platform ranks sellers of the chosen product | Documented or inferred: Documented | Key measured drivers: Availability, price, quality, primary-seller status; merchant order "predominantly determined by these providers" | Representative evidence: OpenAI Help; PPC Land

A workable formal model treats the probability that a given product is recommended as a product of stage-conditional probabilities: P(recommend) = P(reaches the model) × P(survives source trust | reached) × P(in shortlist | trusted) × P(final pick | shortlisted). The decomposition matters because the levers differ at each link and because failure is overwhelmingly concentrated at the first one. In a cross-provider audit of 7,763 cases where neither ChatGPT nor Claude recommended a brand, both diagnosed the same failure mode 95.1% of the time, and the dominant mode was discoverability (the brand never reached the model) rather than compellingness (reached, not mentioned) or positioning (mentioned, not recommended); agreement rose from 81% for category leaders to 99.6% for long-tail regional brands (Jack et al., arXiv 2606.26116).
The one cross-provider estimate puts Claude recommending "from priors" 43–52% of the time versus 8–29% for ChatGPT (arXiv 2606.26116).

Estimates of how often ChatGPT searches the web at all range from 14.4% of responses in Ahrefs' 66.6 million logged-out GPT-5.6 responses (Ahrefs) through 23% (Texta), 31% (Nectiv) and 58% (Graphite) to 80.5% (Cloro), all from GEO vendors with incompatible methods (Texta; Graphite; Cloro).

The zero-shot ranking literature established early that LLM rankers favor popular items in proportion to their frequency (Hou et al., ECIR 2024), and the Ahrefs correlation data are consistent with this: across 75,000 brands, branded web mentions correlated with AI Overview visibility at Spearman 0.664, against 0.326 for Domain Rating and 0.218 for backlinks (Ahrefs).
Product parameters explained 82.4% of ranking variance, list position 6.5%, and brand identity only 1.2% (arXiv 2606.17443).

The same hypersensitivity shows up in the Columbia/Yale ACES sandbox, where a +0.1 rating lifts a 10%-baseline product to 15.4% (Claude Sonnet 4), 20.3% (GPT-4.1) or 16.0% (Gemini 2.5 Flash), and doubling the review count buys price headroom of 17–37% (ACES).
In mid-2025 Wikipedia was ChatGPT's single largest source at 7.8% of all citations and Reddit was Perplexity's at 6.6% (Profound)

by September 2025 ChatGPT's Reddit citations had collapsed from roughly 60% of responses to about 10% within six weeks (Semrush), and by late September 2026 Reddit appeared in about 1 in 43 ChatGPT answers (down 88% from March) while PubMed rose from 64th to 4th most-cited domain and hands-on testers like RTINGS gained (Ahrefs).

Google's two AI surfaces gave answers with 86% semantic similarity to the same queries but cited the same URLs only ~13% of the time (Ahrefs), and ChatGPT and Gemini shared only 5.4% of cited domains for the same commercial query, with zero overlap in 76.7% of comparisons (Uberti-Bona Marin et al., arXiv 2609.18729).

Authority is a weak gate: 47.9% of 20.5 million citations went to domains with DA under 40 (Wellows), programmatic spam sites took more than 14% of ChatGPT citations for B2B "best" prompts (Overthink Group), and cited Reddit posts had a median of 5–8 upvotes with semantic similarity to the answer, not engagement, predicting inclusion (Semrush).

First, licensing buys retrieval prominence on ChatGPT specifically: OpenAI-licensed publishers earned 10.2 citations per cited page versus 6.9 for unlicensed (+48%), OpenAI-exclusive publishers +112%, while Google-licensed publishers showed no AI Overviews premium and Perplexity licensees were at parity (Otterly/Press Ranger).

Second, citation is not recommendation: 61.7% of 3,981 cited domain appearances were "ghost citations" in which the brand was never named, and only 13.2% were both cited and mentioned (Semrush/Indig).
In a 1,094-category study, only 21% of the most-cited domains were also the most-mentioned brand, with a slight negative correlation (−0.229) between the two (Semrush).

In 2,961 volunteer runs of 12 brand-recommendation prompts across ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI, the chance of the same brand list on two runs was under 1 in 100 and the same order under 1 in 1,000; yet in 994 headphone answers Bose, Sony, Sennheiser and Apple each appeared in 55–77% of responses, tight categories (cloud providers) were stable, and broad ones (sci-fi novels) scattered (SparkToro).

Repeated-query studies show the brand set converging: ten calls recovered 92.6–95.2% of the fifteen-call brand set across 4,500 responses (Żatuchin, arXiv 2609.05059), and a generalizability analysis of ~190,000 observations found five runs reach a coefficient of 0.96 across 250 questions even though a single Gemini question scored 0.27 (arXiv 2609.04047).

Daily tracking of 1,300+ commercial prompts over 28 days found only a quarter of ChatGPT's cited pages reappeared the next day, but the most frequently named brand appeared on 82% of days (89% for AI Overviews) (Detailed).

Cross-model disagreement exceeds within-model noise: ChatGPT and Claude recommendation sets overlapped with Jaccard 0.35 against a same-prompt rerun baseline of 0.50–0.61 (arXiv 2606.26116), API outputs overlapped only 12–15% with the same vendor's consumer interface (arXiv 2609.18729), and model updates act as demand shocks: the Fitbit Inspire was chosen 45% of the time by Claude Sonnet 4, 77% by Claude Opus 4.5 and 6% by GPT-5.1 from the same assortment (ACES).

All tested models over-select the top row of a results grid, but the favored column differs by model (GPT-4.1 first column, Claude middle columns, Gemini columns 3–4); for Claude Sonnet 4, moving a product from bottom-right (4.5% selection) to the top row raised selection about fivefold, a move worth roughly a doubling of price, and the effect persisted under "ignore position" instructions and in headless JSON interfaces; GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.1 showed nearly opposite position preferences (ACES).
An "Overall Pick" badge raised a 10% baseline to 24.3%, 19.9% and 42.6% across the three models, while a "Sponsored" tag lowered it to 8.9%, 8.0% and 7.9% (ACES).

In Microsoft's Magentic Marketplace simulation, customer agents accepted the first proposal received 80–100% of the time (Claude Sonnet 4.5 93.3%, GPT-4o 100%), and consumer welfare fell for nearly every model as the number of visible businesses rose from 3 to 100 (Claude Sonnet 4 from 1,800 to 600 against an optimum near 2,200) because agents explored too few options (Microsoft Research).
Agents also concentrate: choices cluster on a few "modal" products with some brands never chosen, a "departure from human consumers, whose preferences are more dispersed" (ACES).

quotes.quote: departure from human consumers, whose preferences are more dispersed

claims.text: The one documented defense sits with the consumer rather than the seller: explicit user profiles "act as switches that override other cues" (ABxLab), and stating a precise criterion restored agent optimality from 0.29–0.48 to 0.83–0.88 under costly inspection (Tool-Lab, arXiv 2609.28372).

quotes.quote: act as switches that override other cues

claims.text: The 30-bias benchmark that tested 20 models in 30,000 scenarios found evidence of every bias in some model, but status quo bias and the disposition effect were the only two with negative averages, and bias did not correlate with model size or capability (Malberg et al.).

The Wharton persuasion studies establish that Cialdini's principles exist in the weights: seven principles more than doubled GPT-4o-mini's compliance with objectionable requests (33.3% to 72.0%), and on Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5 mini and Gemini 3 Flash with reasoning enabled the lift shrank to 35.3% to 51.3% but stayed positive in all 21 model-by-principle cells (Wharton GAIL 2025; Wharton GAIL 2026, PNAS).

Principle or bias: Social proof (Cialdini) | Verdict for AI agents: Works, harder than on humans | Effect size and models: One expert-written sentence raised recommendation rate +42.1 points on Claude 3.7, +40.1 LLaMA-70B, +334% relative on Claude 3.5; still +14.8 with Claude 3.7 extended thinking; offsets a ~0.27-star deficit. "Best seller"/"purchased by 50,000+" shifted choice 10–60 pp in 14/17 models (Claude Sonnet 4 +55.9, GPT-5 +53.3) vs humans +9.9. Breakthrough vs incumbent 50.7% | Source: Bias Beware; ABxLab; arXiv 2606.17443

Principle or bias: Authority (Cialdini) | Verdict for AI agents: Works when it is a recognized third party or evidence claim; authoritative tone backfires | Effect size and models: Wirecutter-pick cue was the largest ABxLab nudge; authority language broke the incumbent monopoly 73.3% of runs, worth ≈ +0.17 stars or a 15.3% discount (GPT-4o-mini, claude-sonnet-4-6, gemini-3-flash-preview). But "Authoritative" tone was negative on all five E-GEO engines (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash, DeepSeek V3.2, Llama 4 Maverick) and not significant in the Princeton GEO paper | Source: ABxLab; arXiv 2606.17443; E-GEO; GEO

Principle or bias: Scarcity / urgency (Cialdini) | Verdict for AI agents: Null or backfires | Effect size and models: "Only few items left" cut Claude 3.5's recommendation rate −13.5 points (≈ −30% relative); exclusivity −30 to −44.6 points on Claude 3.7; "Only X remaining" weakly negative in ACES across Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash; breakthrough vs incumbent only 11.7% | Source: Bias Beware; ACES; arXiv 2606.17443

Principle or bias: Commitment, unity, liking, reciprocity (Cialdini) | Verdict for AI agents: Strong for compliance, not seller-stageable | Effect size and models: Commitment 47% → 83%, unity 23% → 45%, liking 19% → 26%, reciprocity 24% → 31% compliance on 2025–26 reasoning models; these require a conversational set-up a product page cannot provide | Source: Wharton GAIL 2026

Principle or bias: Platform endorsement badge | Verdict for AI agents: Works, large | Effect size and models: "Overall Pick": 10% → 24.3% (Claude Sonnet 4), 19.9% (GPT-4.1), 42.6% (Gemini 2.5 Flash); price headroom +65–138% | Source: ACES
Principle or bias: "Sponsored" label | Verdict for AI agents: Backfires | Effect size and models: 10% → 8.9% / 8.0% / 7.9% across the same three models | Source: ACES

Principle or bias: Star rating (+0.1) | Verdict for AI agents: Works, far harder than on humans | Effect size and models: Higher-rated option gained 30–80 pp in 14/17 models (o4-mini 81.2, o3 77.6, GPT-5 61.8) vs humans +5.0; +0.1 star lifts 10% → 15.4–20.3%; failure to notice +0.1 fell from 71.7% (GPT-4o) to under 1.7% in latest models | Source: ABxLab; ACES

Principle or bias: Review count | Verdict for AI agents: Works | Effect size and models: Doubling reviews buys 17–37% price headroom; fictional brand wins 50% at 1.6× reviews | Source: ACES; arXiv 2606.17443

Principle or bias: Framed discount vs real price cut (Thaler/Kahneman reference price) | Verdict for AI agents: Framing works; charm prices do not | Effect size and models: "~26% off" text raised rate +23.0 (LLaMA-70B) and +37.4 (Claude 3.7) and beat an actual 50% price cut in most models; but 7 of 8 2026 models weighted cents like dollars and 6 of 8 weighted "20% off" the same as a list-price cut | Source: Bias Beware; Tool-Lab

Principle or bias: "Free" / BOGO / free shipping (Ariely zero-price) | Verdict for AI agents: Works | Effect size and models: BOGO and free shipping shifted choice 10–60 pp when ratings/prices matched; BOGO moved 40.6% on cell phones, 60.9% on cookies | Source: ABxLab

Principle or bias: Decoy / asymmetric dominance (Ariely) | Verdict for AI agents: Weak, inconsistent | Effect size and models: Positive for GPT-4 in 5/6 hiring occupations; for gpt-4o-mini subscriptions the target's share did not rise (24 → 23/50) and the decoy itself was picked 14%; "mixed or inconsistent" as a description injection on Claude 3.5/3.7 and Llama 8–405B; no Economist-style replication on a frontier model | Source: arXiv 2409.15299; NHSJS; Bias Beware

Principle or bias: Anchoring (Kahneman) | Verdict for AI agents: Works in negotiation and numeric hints; untested for posted MSRP | Effect size and models: Seller opening above target raised seller utility 0.37 (GPT-4o), 0.54 (GPT-4), 0.63 (Llama-3); o1 lost as much as GPT-4o unless warned; anchoring was the only one of six biases with human direction (d = 1.89) and extra reasoning did not reduce it | Source: arXiv 2508.21137; Kraishan

Principle or bias: Attribute / gain-loss framing (Kahneman) | Verdict for AI agents: Present but direction unstable; near-absent in reasoning models | Effect size and models: Δ(admit−reject) +0.165 GPT-3.5 vs −0.405 GPT-4; gpt-4o-mini 66% vs 42% acceptance by frame; reasoning models (GPT-5.1, DeepSeek-R1) correlate 0.86–1.00 with expected payoff and are "largely insensitive" to framing, conversational models < 0.5 | Source: Echterhoff; NHSJS; Mind the (DH) Gap

Principle or bias: Loss aversion / "final sale" | Verdict for AI agents: Weak for sellers | Effect size and models: GPT-4o ignored expected value in >95% of loss vignettes, but negative-framing cues ("final sale", "newer version available") were not among ABxLab's movers; breakthrough vs incumbent 9.6% | Source: arXiv 2410.02820; ABxLab; arXiv 2606.17443

Principle or bias: Status quo / default (Thaler) | Verdict for AI agents: Present in simulations; mixed for agents | Effect size and models: Large positive status-quo coefficients in every model from GPT-4 (0.93) to GPT-4o (0.32) in budget tasks; but the 30-bias benchmark finds a negative average (preference for change) | Source: Horton; Malberg

Principle or bias: Hedonic vs functional context (Ariely relativity) | Verdict for AI agents: Works | Effect size and models: Every one of 12 models (incl. GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.5 Flash) chose the premium option more than 2× as often under hedonic cues; thinking mode did not reduce it | Source: arXiv 2609.22225

Principle or bias: Position / primacy | Verdict for AI agents: Works, large, model-specific direction | Effect size and models: Top-row premium in all ACES models; "viewed first" effect ranged from −35.4 pp (Claude 3.5 Haiku) to +88.8 pp (GPT-4.1 Nano) vs humans +4.0; on 100-listing hotel pages agents showed a mid-list dip that higher reasoning effort removed | Source: ACES; ABxLab; arXiv 2608.22697

Principle or bias: Choice overload (Iyengar/Schwartz) | Verdict for AI agents: Works, in the agent's own exploration | Effect size and models: Welfare fell as options rose from 3 to 100 because agents inspected too few; no study of overload-induced deferral found | Source: Microsoft Research

Principle or bias: Fabricated citations / bandwagon statistics | Verdict for AI agents: Works on judges; weak on product rank | Effect size and models: Fake references dropped every judge but GPT-4o below random; "85% of people believe" swayed ChatGPT 86% of the time but GPT-4 0%; any citation, real or fake, raised acceptance 3–22 points across 220,564 prompts; yet adding statistics to product text lowered rank in 19 of 24 settings | Source: Chen et al.; CoBBLEr; AuthorityBench; C-SEO Bench

Principle or bias: User memory / stated preference (sycophancy) | Verdict for AI agents: Works, strongest single lever found | Effect size and models: "I love hiking!" redirected most 2026 agents away from an objectively superior product (Claude Opus 4.8 picked the hiking watch ~75% of runs); only Gemini 3.5 Flash unaffected | Source: Wharton GAIL

Principle or bias: Prompt injection in page text | Verdict for AI agents: Works, model-dependent, a policy violation | Effect size and models: Redirected all payments for GPT-4o, GPT-OSS-20b, Qwen3-4b; Claude Sonnet 4 resisted; hidden text in reviews/metadata succeeded 41.7–68.2% in StakeBench; agents start following injections 16–86% but complete the goal 0–17% | Source: Microsoft Research; CSO Online; WASP
Principle or bias: Keyword stuffing | Verdict for AI agents: Backfires | Effect size and models: −8.7% to −9.1% visibility | Source: GEO

Numeric rationality improved sharply: failure to pick a 1%-cheaper identical item fell from over 63% (Claude Sonnet 3.5) to about 9% (GPT-4.1), and the latest models "almost never" miss price differences (ACES)
reasoning-trained models are near expected-value maximizers on risky choice (Mind the (DH) Gap)
and frontier agents resisted fake awards and fake reviews that fooled small open-weight models (Microsoft Research).
But preference-ordering biases with no normative answer did not shrink: reasoning siblings were not less biased than non-reasoning ones (Δ = +0.031 toward more bias) (Kraishan)
o3 and o4-mini showed the largest rating effects and still 38–48 pp nudge effects with ratings matched (ABxLab)
large reasoning models "show no improvement in robustness" to bandwagon cues on subjective tasks (arXiv 2504.09946)
and a "focus only on product features" system prompt left social-proof effects of +19.75 to +23.38 points intact (Bias Beware).

Because pretraining backbone, not fine-tuning, is the main determinant of a model's bias profile (arXiv 2507.07186), and because non-RLHF Mistral Large showed the same social-proof effect as RLHF models, part of the susceptibility is baked in at pretraining and will not be removed by alignment alone.

On unbranded discovery prompts, brand-owned domains receive 2.24% of citations versus 30.7% on branded prompts (a 13.7× gap), and 85% of unbranded responses cited no brand-owned source at all, across 57.2 million citations (AirOps/Foundation).

For 2,000 "best product" questions across five engines, 70% of 17,524 answers cited at least one affiliate review site (Perplexity 99.4%, AI Overviews 79.3%, ChatGPT 61%, Gemini 54.7%), led by Forbes 14.4%, Wirecutter 10.3%, Consumer Reports 7.6%, TechRadar 7.3%, CNET 7.2%, Tom's Guide 7.2% and RTINGS 7.0% (Suff Digital).

In 3,312 product-intent responses across consumer electronics, wearables and home categories, the top sources were YouTube 19%, Reddit 19%, RTINGS 16%, Forbes 9%, PCMag 8% and CNET 8%, and the authors wrote that "Brand-owned domains are conspicuously absent from the top of this list" (Cloro.dev).

quotes.quote: Brand-owned domains are conspicuously absent from the top of this list

claims.text: Listicles took 40.9% of commercial-intent citations versus 21.9% overall (Wix Studio).

The closest thing to a quantified absence penalty is observational: when neither the brand nor its domain appeared in the retrieval path, the brand was mentioned in 2.8% (GPT) and 3.8% (Gemini) of answers; with an own-domain citation present, 49.0% and 58.4% (Tannenbaum, arXiv 2609.23162).

And the controlled agent evidence shows how heavily a recognized reviewer weighs once retrieved: a single Wirecutter screenshot moved Gemini 3.5 Flash +99 points toward Wirecutter's pick, Wirecutter dominated Reddit and The Strategist for both Claude models, and a Reddit-plus-Strategist combination moved no model (Wharton GAIL)
in ABxLab, the Wirecutter-pick cue was the single largest nudge across 17 models (ABxLab).

Finally, ChatGPT's own fan-out queries for running shoes contained "best" 206 times and "review" 117 times but "official" only 65 times (Ahrefs), meaning the engine actively goes looking for third-party verdicts.

Branded and factual queries are not walled. Official websites supplied 63.4% of ChatGPT citations for factual questions (pricing, features) and still 46.4% for comparison questions; brand site: searches made up 75.9% of ChatGPT's fan-out searches to the most-searched domains, with apple.com, ikea.com, nike.com and samsung.com at the top (Ahrefs).
Local and listings-heavy queries drew 86% "brand-managed" citations (Yext).

Gemini and Google AI Overviews are the most vendor-site-friendly engines, with roughly three-quarters of their top-100 cited domains being vendors against one-quarter for ChatGPT and Perplexity (Overthink Group).

Niche categories have thin corpora and open slots. Only 15.2% of 1,094 ChatGPT categories had a clear owner, 53.7% were unsettled, and high-demand topics were more open (11.3% owned) than low-demand ones (19%) (Semrush).

Across 3,750 responses on 250 category queries, 8.0% of queries were "competitive vacuums" concentrated in narrow segments (luxury fashion online CVI 0.87, "Electronics in Nordics" 0.73), the three models agreed on the top brand in only 41.6% of queries, and brands absent from 33–38 of 50 queries still achieved total ownership on specific ones (arXiv 2606.23057).
SparkToro's tight-market finding (LA Volvo dealers and cloud providers consistent, broad categories scattered) points the same way (SparkToro).

Even in mass-market electronics the top product (Garmin Forerunner 265) appeared in only ~2% of responses, with a product HHI of 0.0005 (Cloro.dev), so the barrier there is not a single incumbent but the depth of the third-party corpus that assembles a wide, churning shortlist.

Feeds and Google Shopping are a side door for product cards. In ChatGPT, 87.3% of 812,190 product cards came from web crawl and 12.7% from direct merchant feeds (Profound), and the top ChatGPT product appeared in Google Shopping's first three results 75% of the time across 100 prompts × 5 runs (Semrush).

Google states there are "no additional requirements" beyond being indexed and snippet-eligible to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode (Google Search Central), and Perplexity's CEO said merchants in its free program get "increased chances of being a recommended product" because richer data helps judge relevance (Fortune).

quotes.quote: increased chances of being a recommended product

claims.text: Review volume and rating on retail surfaces substitute for editorial authority. Top-ranked ChatGPT product cards had a median of 787 reviews versus 352 for bottom-ranked (Profound)
Amazon Rufus essentially never recommends products below 4.0 stars (median 4.5) across 1,300+ recommended products (PPC Land/Amalytix)
and the controlled experiments show 1.6× reviews or +0.075 stars is enough to beat a familiar brand (arXiv 2606.17443).
Retailer pages are themselves third-party sources: Best Buy appeared in 12% of electronics responses and Walmart in 11% (Cloro.dev).

The wall itself is unstable and low-fidelity. Reddit's ChatGPT citation share swung from ~60% of responses to ~10% in six weeks (Semrush) and then fell 88% over 2026 as primary sources, brand support pages and hands-on testers rose (Ahrefs).

An obscure site (Toxigon) sat in ChatGPT's all-time top 10 cited domains in 2025 (Profound), and ~16% of sources cited across four engines showed signs of being AI-generated (Allaham & Diakopoulos, AIES 2026).
Licensing does not even guarantee that a publisher's verdicts are reported correctly: ChatGPT linked to WIRED's buying guides while naming picks that were not in them (TechBuzz summary).

But no dataset shows Wirecutter as a gatekeeper of the candidate set: it is one of seven publishers in the 7–14% band on "best product" answers (behind Forbes), RTINGS rather than Wirecutter dominates the electronics data, Wirecutter's parent is litigating against OpenAI while Condé Nast, Dotdash Meredith and Axel Springer titles plausibly enjoy a ChatGPT licensing premium, and the Ahrefs correlation ordering (branded web mentions 0.664 > branded search volume 0.392 > DR 0.326) describes breadth of presence rather than any single endorsement (Ahrefs).

Two small-retailer findings bound the realistic outcome for a company that gets in without marquee coverage: small retailers were cited about as often as chains but chains received ~2.5× the leading recommendations and small stores got about 1 in 10 first-place slots on specific queries (Lightspeed-sponsored) (Fit Small Business), and a practitioner's three-month, 50-query tracking of a small B2B client logged 4 mentions against 47 for the market leader (Roberto Serra).

Tactic: Earn genuine review volume and ≥4.0 rating on retailer and marketplace pages | Evidence status: Measured (correlational + controlled) | What the data show: 787 vs 352 median reviews top vs bottom cards; Rufus 4.0-star floor; 1.6× reviews or +0.075 stars beats a familiar brand in controlled tests | Risk: Low if authentic (Profound; PPC Land; arXiv 2606.17443)

Tactic: Google Merchant Center / Shopify / OpenAI feed hygiene | Evidence status: Measured for eligibility, not rank | What the data show: 75% of top ChatGPT products in Google Shopping top-3; feeds supply 12.7% of cards and live price/availability; nine required fields, aggregate reviewcount and starrating only | Risk: Low (Semrush; Profound; OpenAI spec)

Tactic: Complete, structured, factual product attributes and self-contained answer passages | Evidence status: Measured, modest | What the data show: Removing a key attribute cuts selection 20–40%; complete machine-readable attributes beat stronger marketing; LLM-rewritten listings +0.56 rank (GPT-5); structural-field enrichment ~+22% retrieval (secondary) | Risk: Low (Kantar on ACES; E-GEO; Ottmann on SAGEO)

Tactic: Target a narrow sub-category with a small candidate pool | Evidence status: Measured (observational) | What the data show: 8% of queries are competitive vacuums; 53.7% of categories unsettled; tight markets stable across runs | Risk: Low (arXiv 2606.23057; Semrush)

Tactic: Authentic third-party coverage: hands-on testers, YouTube, retailer and forum presence | Evidence status: Measured correlation only | What the data show: Branded web mentions 0.664, YouTube mentions ~0.74 with AI visibility; no controlled study shows that manufacturing mentions causes recommendations | Risk: Low if earned (Ahrefs; Ahrefs)

Tactic: Legitimate social-proof and evidence statements on PDPs ("best-selling", verifiable test results) | Evidence status: Measured in sandboxes | What the data show: +42 points for one truthful social-proof sentence; authority claims worth ≈ +0.17 stars; but fabricated clinical claims also worked, and FTC rules apply | Risk: Medium: must be true and substantiated (Bias Beware; arXiv 2606.17443)

Tactic: Labelled ads in ChatGPT, Rufus, AI Mode | Evidence status: Platform-documented | What the data show: Separate "Sponsored" units; agents penalize sponsored tags (10% → 7.9–8.9%); no evidence of leakage into organic | Risk: Budget question, not visibility (Common Thread tracker; ACES)

Tactic: Digital PR / earned media "85% off-site" | Evidence status: Vendor-asserted | What the data show: Indig's 85% figure has no published methodology; Muck Rack's 84% earned-media citation share uses a broad definition | Risk: Unknown (Previsible; Muck Rack)

Tactic: schema.org Product/Review/FAQ markup | Evidence status: Vendor-asserted | What the data show: Google: "no special schema.org structured data that you need to add"; one weak agency test | Risk: None, but unproven (Google Search Central)

claims.text: Tactic: llms.txt | Evidence status: Measured: no effect | What the data show: No correlation across ~300,000 domains; 97% of 137,210 files got zero bot requests | Risk: None, wasted effort (DEV/Ahrefs/SE Ranking)

Tactic: GEO tone tricks: authoritative voice, added statistics, keyword stuffing | Evidence status: Measured: null or negative on 2025–26 models | What the data show: Only 3 of 54 C-SEO cases positive; statistics lowered rank in 19 of 24 settings; authoritative tone negative on all five E-GEO engines; keyword stuffing −9%; body-text GEO cut top-10 retrieval 16% in SAGEO Arena | Risk: Visibility loss (C-SEO Bench; E-GEO; PPC Land on Martinez survey)

Tactic: Scarcity, urgency, exclusivity copy | Evidence status: Measured: backfires | What the data show: −13.5 to −44.6 points on Claude 3.5/3.7; weakly negative in ACES | Risk: Visibility loss (Bias Beware)

Tactic: Reddit / UGC seeding | Evidence status: Correlational pull; measured enforcement | What the data show: Reddit: "no guarantee that what is on Reddit will make its way into LLMs"; Trap Plan exposed for 100 fake accounts; r/Biohackers moratorium over AEO abuse | Risk: High: account purges, public exposure (AdExchanger; Kotaku)

quotes.quote: no guarantee that what is on Reddit will make its way into LLMs

claims.text: Tactic: Fake or AI-generated reviews, bought sentiment, fake awards | Evidence status: Measured to work on weak models only | What the data show: Frontier agents (Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash) resisted fake awards and reviews | Risk: High: FTC rule with civil penalties, warning letters Dec 2025 (FTC; Microsoft Research)

Tactic: Hidden text / prompt injection on product pages | Evidence status: Measured to work, model-dependent | What the data show: 41.7–68.2% success in StakeBench; superlative/emotional copy flagged 99–100% by a simple defense | Risk: High: cloaking under Google spam policy as of May 2026; security exploit (CSO Online; E-GEO; PPC Land)

The FTC's Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (final August 2024) bans fake or AI-generated reviews, sentiment-conditioned compensation, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled "independent" review sites and review suppression, with civil penalties for knowing violators (FTC)
warning letters went to ten companies in December 2025 (DLA Piper).

Google's May 15, 2026 changelog made explicit that all spam policies, including cloaking for AI crawlers, scaled AI content and inauthentic brand mentions, apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode (PPC Land).
Reddit is detecting and removing coordinated inauthentic accounts and has publicly questioned "the legitimacy of any provider suggesting they can" guarantee LLM pickup (AdExchanger).

quotes.quote: the legitimacy of any provider suggesting they can

claims.text: The Incumbent Advantage paper adds a game-theoretic warning for even the legitimate text levers: when all nine fictional brands adopted the same authority language, the individual payoff fell from +0.802 to +0.007, the incumbent recovered to 93.8%, and non-adopters received zero recommendations across 4,745 trials (arXiv 2606.17443), which C-SEO Bench independently describes as a "congested, zero-sum game" (C-SEO Bench).

AI-referred traffic to US retailers grew 393% year over year in Q1 2026 and converted 42% more often than non-AI traffic (reversing a 38% deficit a year earlier) [vendor/secondary] (Digital Commerce 360 on Adobe), and after OpenAI made brand links more prominent in May 2026 the share of ChatGPT referrals landing on brand homepages jumped from ~26–32% to ~60% [vendor/secondary] (Similarweb summaries).

Publishers are being read far more than visited (Anthropic's crawl-to-referral ratio was ~38,000:1 and OpenAI's ~1,100:1 in mid-2025, from secondary compilations of Cloudflare data) (SEOmator), and RTINGS paywalled its full test data in March 2026 citing uncredited AI scraping (Wikipedia: RTINGS).
